title: Meta’s Muse Could Upend All Kinds of Businesses. It Hasn’t Yet
gist: Meta claims its Muse shopping agent has 10M+ activated users in the US and Canada with over 25% using it to shop at $200+ average purchases, but executives at ~50 companies including DoorDash, Hilton, T-Mobile and eBay report agent-driven activity as negligible. Zuckerberg plans transaction fees he says could eventually top Meta's ad business, while companies like Chipotle, Costco and Amazon adjust their stances toward agents.

insights.claim: Mark Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the US and Canada had activated Muse, with over 25 percent using it for shopping, more than any other task and above Meta's expectations.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Shopping is Meta's lead use case for agents; track activation and conversion disclosures on future earnings calls.

insights.claim: Meta claims millions of people use Muse to make purchases averaging more than $200, and it has partnerships with 10 retailers including Walmart, Best Buy, and Gap.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Partner retailers' upcoming earnings are the first independent check on Meta's agentic commerce claims.

insights.claim: Zuckerberg said Meta plans to charge businesses a fee on transactions facilitated by Muse and predicted this revenue would eventually exceed Meta's advertising business.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: A take-rate model on agentic commerce would be a new revenue pillar for Meta and a margin cost for merchants.

insights.claim: Executives at roughly 50 companies across travel, telecom, food, and self-storage shrugged off near-term disruption from AI shopping agents, and many said they would mostly benefit from widespread adoption.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Wall Street's fear of agent-driven margin compression is not yet visible in company data.

insights.claim: DoorDash put agent orders in the 'hundreds', Hilton called agent bookings 'insignificant', T-Mobile saw nothing of significance, Ally Financial called it 'quite low', and eBay said 'very, very small'.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Agentic commerce volumes are currently immaterial to merchant results, a gap versus Meta's headline claims.

insights.claim: Despite expectations that users would ask agents to cancel unused subscriptions, Life Time Group reported zero agent cancellations, Public Storage and Hartford Insurance gave similar data, and India's Eternal put agentic commerce at close to zero.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: The feared subscription-churn threat from agents has not materialized for recurring-revenue businesses yet.

insights.claim: DoorDash CEO and Meta board member Tony Xu said present hype about agents might be 'delusional', even as DoorDash works on agent readiness.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Skepticism from a Meta board member tempers the bull case for near-term agent commerce.

insights.claim: Chipotle found agents failing to complete orders due to loyalty-discount and after-hours issues; Muse's debut raised agentic orders by a single-digit percentage, and Chipotle is cleaning up its site code for agents.

insights.so_what: Agent-readiness of web checkout is becoming a new digital operations priority for consumer brands.

insights.claim: Costco and Extra Space Storage report surging sales originating from chatbots like Gemini and ChatGPT as they optimize content for them, and plan to do the same for AI agents.

insights.so_what: Chatbot referral traffic is a nearer-term commerce channel than autonomous agents; optimization spend is shifting toward it.

insights.claim: Many executives dismissed the risk that agents' comparison shopping will erode profits, arguing product quality, customer service, and brand trust will still drive purchases.

insights.claim: Amazon blocked Muse last month, arguing users preferred its own Alexa shopping agent, but this week said it anticipates working with outside agents; Insurify similarly reversed its block after adding tech to ensure accurate agent offers.
insights.speaker: Paresh Dave
insights.so_what: Rapid reversals suggest walled-garden resistance to third-party agents is weakening, widening Muse's addressable market.
insights.locator: Stances on agents are evolving quickly
